findings.title: --require-pgp can be bypassed: unsigned text placed BEFORE the signed block is parsed as checksums while gpg still reports GOODSIG
findings.location: signed_body() 277-284, parse_sha256sums() 287-293, pgp_check() 365-386, used by resolve_kernel() 345-351 and fetch_source() 462-465
findings.scenario: Threat model is the one --require-pgp exists for: whoever controls what cdn.kernel.org (or a TLS-inspecting corporate proxy) serves. 1) They serve sha256sums.asc = the line 'x-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----', an empty line, '<evil sha>  linux-7.2.6.tar.xz', then the untouched genuine kernel.org file. 2) signed_body()'s regex is not anchored to a line start, so re.search matches the fake header first; the lazy (.*?) runs up to the GENUINE '-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----', so the captured 'signed body' contains the evil line first and the real lines after it. 3) parse_sha256sums() is 'first wins' -> the evil hash. 4) gpg ignores everything before the first real armor line, verifies the genuine block and prints GOODSIG+VALIDSIG -> pgp_check() returns 'good'. 5) fetch_source() prints 'PGP : sha256sums.asc signed by <kernel.org signer>', download() enforces the ATTACKER's sha256, and the tarball is extracted, built and later installed as root. The existing guard (and its unit test, test_tool.py 504) only covers text appended AFTER the signature.
findings.evidence:
Experiment with throw-away keyrings in my scratch dir (victim keyring holds only the 'genuine' signer), gpg 2.4.5:
  pgp_check      -> ('good', 'Kernel Autosigner <autosigner@example.invalid>')
  parsed sums    -> {'7.2.6': 'eeeeeeee...'}      (genuine file alone gives 'aaaa...')
End to end through resolve_kernel('7.2.6', ...): target['sha256'] = 'eeeeeeeeeeeeeeee...' and pgp_check(target['signed_text']) = 'good'.
Code: 282  m = re.search(r"-----BEGIN PGP SIGNED MESSAGE-----\r?\n(?:[^\r\n]+\r?\n)*\r?\n(.*?)" ...   (no ^ / re.M);  291  if m and m.group(2) not in sums:   # first wins
Not exploitable variants I also tried: attacker-signed block + genuine block (gpg aborts with 'multiple plaintexts seen' -> not 'good'); anchored fake header with a bogus armor line (gpg fails -> 'unavailable').
findings.suggested_fix: Do not re-derive the signed region with a regex; use the text gpg itself verified. In pgp_check run gpg with '--output <tmpfile> --decrypt' (tested here: the output file contains only the genuine signed lines and GOODSIG/VALIDSIG are still emitted), return that plaintext, and in fetch_source when state == 'good' require parse_sha256sums(verified_plaintext).get(version) == target['sha256'], else raise. Minimum stop-gap: anchor the regex with (?m)^ and refuse a file whose first non-empty line is not the armor header.

findings.title: A --modules full build can silently start from this tool's own TRIMMED config in /boot (same-series rule ignores want_full)
findings.location: find_base_config() 1533-1540 (the same-series shortcut returns before the want_full guard at 1541-1545); the trimmed config gets into /boot via install_kernel() 2825-2826
findings.scenario: 1) User installs a trimmed 7.2.x kernel with this tool; install always writes /boot/config-7.2.6-gpu (trimmed, ~140 modules). 2) It fails to boot or they simply boot the distro kernel (6.12 el10). 3) They run `build --kernel 7.2.x --modules full` (the safe rebuild, or the kernel meant for publishing). skip_own correctly ignores the tree's own .config, `mine` = /boot/config-6.12.0-...el10 (series 6.12 != 7.2), so the same-series rule fires: close = [the trimmed /boot/config-7.2.6-gpu] and it is returned. The want_full check two lines below is never reached and richest() has only one candidate. Result: a 'full' kernel with ~140 modules that lacks other machines' disk/NIC drivers (and repeats whatever the trimmed kernel was missing). The label printed does not say the config is trimmed. May overlap with the build reader's area; reported because nothing else catches it.
findings.evidence:
Fake root experiment (boot/config-6.12.0-211.53.1.el10_2 with 2507 =m, boot/config-7.2.6-gpu with 140 =m, running=6.12 el10, target_series='7.2', want_full=True):
  base chosen for --modules full: boot/config-7.2.6-gpu with 140 modules
  label: /boot/config-7.2.6-gpu  (a 7.2 config, like this tree -- the running kernel's is 6.12; --config-base running overrides)
The existing test (test_tool.py 528) only covers the case where a full config of the SAME series is also present.
findings.suggested_fix: In the same-series branch, when want_full drop trimmed candidates before choosing: e.g. full = DotConfig(richest(others)).count('m'); close = [c for c in close if not want_full or DotConfig(c).count('m') * 2 >= full]; fall through to the existing logic when close becomes empty.

findings.title: Build is refused over pahole's version (or absence) even though the default --debug-info off never runs pahole; no flag overrides it
findings.location: check_tree_requirements() 1800-1839 (pahole row is never '(optional)' in changes.rst), enforced at cmd_build() 3677-3679 and cmd_plan() 3620-3621
findings.scenario: RHEL 8 (pahole <= 1.25), Debian 12 (1.24), Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 (1.22/1.25), or any box without dwarves: `build --kernel stable` with default options. linux-7.2's own table says 'pahole 1.26'. The default debug_info=off makes build_requests set DEBUG_INFO_BTF=n, so kbuild never invokes pahole (scripts/pahole-version.sh just yields 0). doctor() agrees -- it only wants pahole for btf/on (3469) -- but check_tree_requirements() has no access to opts or the config, treats the row as mandatory, returns 1, and cmd_build raises 'the chosen tools do not meet linux-7.2.6's own minimums'. --yes does not help; the only way out is building a newer pahole for a kernel that will not use it.
findings.evidence:
Row in /home/madness/src/linux-7.2.4/Documentation/process/changes.rst: 'pahole                 1.26             pahole --version' (5.15 has 1.16, also not optional). Experiment with a fake tree holding that changes.rst with the minimum raised above the installed 1.31 (= what an older distro sees):
  FAIL pahole 1.31 is too old: this tree needs >= 9.99  (`pahole --version`)
  ok   13 build tools meet this tree's own minimums (changes.rst)
  -> blocking problems: 1
Code: 1801 'if not prog.startswith(REQ_RELEVANT)' includes 'pahole'; 1803 optional only if '(optional)' in the row; 3677 'if check_tree_requirements(tree, toolchain): raise ToolError'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give check_tree_requirements a need_pahole argument (cmd_build/cmd_plan pass opts['debug_info'] != 'off') and treat the pahole row as optional when it is False: `if name == 'pahole' and not need_pahole: optional = True`.

findings.title: 'Will it boot here' verdict: the root disk's controller/transport driver is never required, and a missing one is only a warning unless >25% of all modules are missing
findings.location: storage_stack() 664-698 (walks to the leaf device, then stops), build_requests() 1357-1372, post_build_checks() 2432-2441
findings.scenario: PLAN 4.4 promises 'build refuses if the config cannot mount this machine's root'. Requests cover the filesystem, dm, dm-crypt and md only. With the default base (the running kernel's config) everything else survives because requests are additive and localmodconfig keeps loaded modules -- I found multipath, iSCSI, bcache, btrfs-raid, stratis, virtio-scsi, storvsc, xen-blkfront, NVMe-oF and eMMC all safe on that path. The hole is any base that is NOT this machine's: a fleet profile with config_base=/srv/golden.config made (or trimmed) on box A with AHCI, replayed on box B whose root sits on megaraid_sas / mpt3sas / nvme / hv_storvsc; or a module localmodconfig could not map. Verification passes (XFS, DM present), module_coverage lists megaraid_sas as missing, but 1 of 120 is 0.8% -> warn only, problems stays 0, `build --install` installs, and the kernel drops to the dracut emergency shell. (The old default entry is kept, so it is recoverable -- hence medium.) x86_64 defconfig is mostly caught by the 25% rule; it has no NVMe, storvsc or xen-blkfront either.
findings.evidence:
Experiment: tree with 119 modules, /proc/modules with those + megaraid_sas ->
  coverage: ['megaraid_sas'] share=0.8% -> post_build_checks counts a problem only if share > 25
Code 2439: `if share > 25: bad(...); problems += 1` is the only path from a missing module to a blocking problem.
findings.suggested_fix: In storage_stack(), for every leaf block device walk up os.path.realpath('/sys/class/block/<leaf>') and collect basename(realpath(<ancestor>/driver/module)) (gives e.g. sd_mod, ahci, megaraid_sas, nvme, virtio_blk, virtio_pci, hv_storvsc, xen_blkfront, mmc_block, sdhci_pci) plus dm_multipath/bcache for those layers; return it as st['modules']. In post_build_checks(): any of those in cov['missing'] -> bad() and problems += 1, whatever the share.

findings.title: Default --gpu auto on a non-x86 machine with no detected GPU makes DRM_I915 a REQUIRED symbol, so the build is always refused
findings.location: resolve_gpu() 1265-1269, build_requests() 1351-1352, verify_requests() 1462-1465, kconfig_symbols() 1197-1206
findings.scenario: aarch64/ppc64le server or cloud VM (BMC or virtio video only; the tool maps these arches in SRCARCH/TRIPLE_ARCH, so they are intended targets). 1) Nothing detected -> vendors = {amd, nvidia, intel} 'so it boots anywhere'. 2) DRM_I915 is added as 'required'. 3) kconfig_symbols() only filters arch/<other>, so drivers/gpu/drm/i915/Kconfig is scanned and DRM_I915 counts as 'defined in this tree'. 4) It 'depends on X86 && PCI', olddefconfig drops it, verify grades it 'fail' (not 'absent'), and cmd_build stops with 'Each FAIL is a dependency that is off, not a typo: make menuconfig' -- advice that cannot work. Same on x86 with a PREEMPT_RT base config (i915 'depends on !PREEMPT_RT'). Only --gpu none/amd,nvidia gets past it, and nothing says so.
findings.evidence:
Experiment (kconfig_symbols on the idle linux-7.2.4 tree with arch='aarch64'):
  gpu=auto, nothing detected -> ['amd', 'intel', 'nvidia']
  DRM_I915     level=required  defined for arm64 tree scan: True
  verify on arm64 when olddefconfig drops it: [('DRM_I915', 'fail')]
drivers/gpu/drm/i915/Kconfig: 'depends on X86 && PCI' / 'depends on !PREEMPT_RT'.
findings.suggested_fix: Vendors that come from the 'none detected' fallback should be requested at level 'wanted', not 'required' (return a flag from resolve_gpu and use it in build_requests); additionally skip 'intel' in the fallback when machine['arch'] is not x86_64/i686.

findings.title: LLVM=<dir>/ and LLVM=-N are passed to kernels older than 5.18, which read them as LLVM=1: the kernel is built by whatever `clang` is first on the scrubbed PATH, and build never checks
findings.location: llvm_companions() 885-889, resolve_toolchain() 1640; no CC_VERSION_TEXT comparison in configure()/cmd_build (only cmd_package 3933 and cmd_pin 4039 have one)
findings.scenario: `build --kernel 5.15 --cc ~/opt/clang-current/bin/clang` (or --cc clang-15 on Debian/Ubuntu). The tool passes LLVM=/home/madness/opt/clang-current/bin/ and, for the prefix form, adds nothing to PATH. Up to v5.17 the top Makefile only tests `ifneq ($(LLVM),)` and sets CC = clang, LD = ld.lld ... by plain name, so with PATH=/usr/bin:... the kernel is compiled by /usr/bin/clang (root's clang 21 here) while the plan, state.ini and the pin all say clang 24 -- exactly 'a build made by a compiler nobody chose' (line 1605). Where no plain `clang` exists the failure is loud but blames a compiler the user never named. The mismatch only surfaces later as a confusing refusal in `package`.
findings.evidence: Fetched from git.kernel.org for confirmation: v5.15 and v5.17 Makefile 426-450: `ifneq ($(LLVM),)` / `HOSTCC = clang` / `CC = clang` / `LD = ld.lld`; v5.18 is the first with `ifneq ($(filter %/,$(LLVM)),)  LLVM_PREFIX := $(LLVM)` / `LLVM_SUFFIX`. Tool: 889 `return "LLVM=" + d + "/", None` (no extra PATH); grep shows CC_VERSION_TEXT is only compared at 3933 and 4036-4039.
findings.suggested_fix: Generic guard, cheap: in configure() after the first olddefconfig compare DotConfig(staging).get('CC_VERSION_TEXT') with the chosen compiler's banner (as cmd_package does) and raise a ToolError naming both. For the old trees themselves: when the tree is < 5.18 and the LLVM argument is not '1', pass LLVM=1 with the clang directory as extra_path (prefix form), or explicit CC=/LD=/AR=/NM=/OBJCOPY=/... HOSTCC=/HOSTCXX= (suffix form).

findings.title: doctor predates signing: a missing signing tool blocks every default build but --install-deps and the printed install line never provide one, and with Secure Boot on it still says the kernel 'is unsigned'
findings.scenario: (a) Fresh Debian / EL-minimal machine, default options (secure_boot=on): `build --install-deps` installs BUILD_DEPS, then doctor adds 'a signing tool' to `missing`, counts a blocking problem, prints the package-manager line WITHOUT any signing package, and cmd_build ends with 'fix them, or re-run with --install-deps to let the package manager try' -- which can never succeed. An unattended fleet replay (`build --profile X --install-deps`) fails on every new machine. The name printed, 'sbsigntools', is also not the Debian/Ubuntu package (sbsigntool). (b) On a machine with Secure Boot enabled, plan/doctor/build print 'a kernel built here is unsigned and will not boot until you sign it or turn Secure Boot off' although this very run signs the image; the step the user really needs is MOK enrolment. The message invites turning Secure Boot off.
findings.evidence:
Experiment (signing_tools() stubbed to '' as on a fresh box; machine secure_boot='on'; default opts):
  FAIL missing: a signing tool (sbsigntools, or pesign + nss-tools)
       sudo apt-get install -y build-essential flex bison bc openssl libssl-dev libelf-dev dwarves libncurses-dev rsync cpio perl python3 xz-utils zstd tar kmod
  warning: Secure Boot is ON: a kernel built here is unsigned and will not boot until you sign it or turn Secure Boot off.
  -> blocking problems: 1
  signing tools named anywhere in BUILD_DEPS? {'dnf': [], 'apt-get': [], 'zypper': [], 'pacman': [], 'yum': []}
findings.suggested_fix: (a) Add the signing packages to BUILD_DEPS (dnf/yum: pesign nss-tools; apt-get: sbsigntool; zypper and pacman: sbsigntools) -- install_deps and the hint then cover it. (b) Make 3527-3529 conditional: with opts['secure_boot']=='on' say the image will be signed with the user's key and must be enrolled once (mokutil --import <der>), and keep the 'unsigned' wording only for --secure-boot off.

findings.title: Root (or an LVM PV) on a PARTITION of an md array -- the normal layout for Intel RST/IMSM BIOS RAID, /dev/md126pN -- loses the RAID-level requirement
findings.location: storage_stack().walk() 675-690
findings.scenario: Workstation/server with firmware RAID1 (mdadm external metadata): / is /dev/md126p3. walk('md126p3') matches ^md\d, but a partition's sysfs directory has neither md/level nor slaves/ (only whole disks do), so the layer becomes 'md:?' and the walk ends. build_requests then requires BLK_DEV_MD but not MD_RAID1, and `detect` shows 'layers md:?'. With the running kernel's config as base nothing is lost, so this only bites together with a foreign/defconfig base -- but that is precisely when the requirement is the thing meant to stop the build.
findings.evidence:
Fake sysfs experiment:
  storage_stack, root on md126p3 : {'rootfs': 'xfs', 'fstypes': ['vfat', 'xfs'], 'layers': ['md:?']}
  md-related requests           : [('BLK_DEV_MD', 'required')]
  control, root on md126        : ['md:raid1'] [('BLK_DEV_MD', 'required'), ('MD_RAID1', 'required')]
findings.suggested_fix: At the top of walk(): `m = re.match(r'^(md\d+)p\d+$', dev)` and, if it matches, `return walk(m.group(1))` -- the whole-disk node has md/level and slaves/.

leftovers.dropped_note:
Seven more, all low. Every experiment used fake roots, throw-away GNUPGHOMEs and a local socket server in my scratch directory. I ran no make and wrote nothing to the live state or keys directories. The `__pycache__` in the project is dated 07:44, before my first import.

**Low-severity items not in the list:**
1. `http_get()` (246) and `download()` (419) catch only `URLError`/`OSError`.
   - A chunked stream that dies raises `http.client.IncompleteRead`, which surfaces as a raw traceback. The `.part` file is left behind but is never renamed, so this is safe.
   - A proxy block page makes `parse_releases()` raise `JSONDecodeError`, also a traceback. I tested both.
2. `--require-pgp` is satisfied silently when the tree already exists. `fetch_source()` returns at 449-451, before any PGP work, even if an earlier run extracted the tree without verification. `pgp_check()` also accepts a good signature from any key in the keyring, not only kernel.org's.
3. `--toolchain llvm` on a box with no clang reports "no working compiler at /usr/bin/gcc" (1619). I tested this.
4. An executable named gcc, clang or python3 that the kernel cannot exec makes `run()` raise an uncaught `OSError(ENOEXEC)`. Examples are a file with no shebang or a foreign-architecture binary in `~/opt` or `~/.local/bin`. It happens inside `detect_machine()`, so every command dies. `run()` at 139 catches only `FileNotFoundError`. I tested this.
5. A relative `--llvm-prefix` is never made absolute (1610-1613), and make runs with `cwd=tree`.
6. `doctor()` checks free space on `--workdir` even when `--source` points to another filesystem (3492).
7. In `extract()`, `os.rename()` onto a tree that a second instance has just created raises a raw `OSError`.

**Python 3.6:** no 3.6 interpreter is installed here. I reasoned from the documentation, an AST scan under 3.12 with `feature_version=(3,6)`, and an inventory of every stdlib attribute and keyword the file uses.
- **API result:** zero hits. There is no walrus, f-string or positional-only parameter, and no `capture_output`, `text=`, `required=`, `filter=`, `shlex.join`, `removeprefix`, `fromisoformat` or `time_ns`. `tarfile` is not imported; extraction uses GNU tar, which strips a leading `/`, rejects `..` and defers symlinks. The newest APIs used are the `errors=` argument to subprocess (3.6), `glob(recursive=)` (3.5) and `os.path.commonpath` (3.5).
- **One behaviour difference:** 3.6 has neither PEP 538 nor PEP 540, so under a C/POSIX locale (cron, systemd, containers) text I/O is ASCII.
  - `out()` guards stdout at line 82, but file writes are unguarded: the build log at 2205-2207, `state.ini` at 2066-2069, `.config` at 1180 and `INSTALL.txt` at 4011.
  - A U+FFFD, which `errors="replace"` decoding introduces, raises `UnicodeEncodeError` on write. In `run_build()` the `except BaseException` handler then terminates make.
  - It is only reachable if build output contains non-ASCII bytes, so it is low.
- **Docstring claim (21-22):** on RHEL 8, dnf depends on `/usr/libexec/platform-python`. `/usr/bin/python3` exists only once a python3x module is installed.

**Checked and found sound:**
- `download()`: `.part` handling, sha mismatch, the short-Content-Length check and re-hashing of a cached tarball.
- `fetch_source()`/`extract()`: the atomic rename and the `.extracting-*` cleanup.
- `resolve_kernel()` selectors.
- `scan_pci()` class and vendor logic.
- dm uuid classification in `storage_stack()`.
- `resolve_toolchain()` argument sets for system gcc, gcc-toolset, private gcc, the clang prefix, suffix and `LLVM=1` forms, ccache and lld, all on kernels 5.18 or newer.
